significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—"velocity and direction of this drift across turns" forecast compliance "several turns before" it occurs—together with a form-(ii) causal claim that a per-turn "restoring force" prevents that same failure while preserving benign utility. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon, namely attack-agnostic pre-compliance drift distinguishable from benign topic drift, and a mechanism that fixes expectations about future turns and identifies when counteracting the trajectory should avert compliance; this directly addresses the action gap exposed by gradual attacks such as Crescendo (Russinovich et al., 2024). A negative result would also be informative by ruling out harmfulness-axis velocity as a robust early-warning variable and/or showing that re-anchoring this representation is not causally sufficient, although it would not rule out multidimensional or non-representational dynamics. Topic substitution fails: deleting the specific trajectory, turns-ahead coupling, and restoring-force mechanism leaves only generic mechanistic LLM safety, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are explicitly the "drift velocity" used as an "attack-agnostic early-warning signal" and the per-turn "restoring-force intervention"; the former is ex ante because it forecasts jailbreaks several turns before compliance, leaving an action window for gating or intervention. Although the harmfulness direction and gain require per-model calibration, the substantive conclusion is a transferable relation—malicious trajectory velocity predicts later compliance and re-anchoring suppresses it—rather than merely a procedure for rediscovering an unrelated direction. Its asserted scope covers multiple kinds of multi-turn attack and white-box models with residual-stream access, so downstream users include researchers as well as deployment or auditing teams able to run an online monitor, but it does not reach black-box deployments and may not cover delayed-onset or drift-aware attacks. Topic substitution fails: generic interpretability-based safety supplies neither this several-turn predictor nor the online control handle, so the reach comes from the claim rather than the topic.
